name: Applicant Flow
who: Businesses of 5–50 staff that hire continuously and lose to bigger employers — hospitality, care, logistics, cleaning, installation.
problem: "We've had the same vacancy up for four months. We get applicants, but not ones we'd hire, and by the time I get round to replying the good ones have taken something else."
solution: We build the recruiting machinery a large employer has and a small one never gets round to: a careers page that sells the job, rewritten ads, distribution to the boards and groups where those people actually look, and an assistant that screens every applicant within the hour, ranks them and books the interview.
promise: The vacancy has been open four months and the applicants worth hiring never reply. A careers page, rewritten ads, and an assistant that screens and books your applicants within the hour — one fixed price per role.
gets:
A careers page built to convert, with a page per open role
Your job ads rewritten and distributed to the boards and groups your candidates use
An assistant that replies within the hour, screens against your criteria and books interviews in your calendar
positioning: Recruiters charge a percentage of salary to find one person. This builds the funnel the business keeps, at a fixed price, and the speed of reply is the product.
voice: Practical and unglamorous. Talks about applicants, replies and interviews booked — never about talent or employer branding.
channels: Sector associations for care and hospitality, LinkedIn to owners and HR of one, payroll and salarisadministratie firms as referrers
